item.title: Intune Connector versions older than 6.2501.2000.5 no longer process Autopilot enrollments — 30 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 30 October 2026

Intune Connector versions older than 6.2501.2000.5 no longer process Autopilot enrollments

The meaningful changes center on enrollment, Apple software updates, and Defender policy planning. Windows Autopilot guidance sets an operational cutoff for older Intune Connector versions, while Intune records the end of legacy ADE authentication and redirects iOS/iPadOS update planning toward DDM controls. Intune also adds in-development and preview Defender policy guidance. Most remaining updates are Configuration Manager and other metadata or link-maintenance edits with no stated administrative action.

Windows Autopilot · Device enrollment

Autopilot connector versions below the cutoff can no longer process enrollments

Updated Connector guidance says Intune Connector for Active Directory versions older than 6.2501.2000.5 are deprecated and can no longer process enrollment requests. It also states that version 6.2504.2001.8 uses WebView2, eliminating the need to disable Internet Explorer Enhanced Security Configuration on Windows Server. Upgrade connectors below the cutoff.

Intune · Device enrollment

Setup Assistant legacy authentication ends for ADE user affinity

Intune says support for Setup Assistant (legacy) authentication with ADE user affinity ended in the October 2026 (2610) service release. Existing profiles are automatically updated to modern authentication, and the legacy option is no longer available. New configurations should use modern authentication with just-in-time registration; no manual migration is stated.

Intune · Device updates

Apple OS 27 moves iOS update control from legacy MDM workloads

The iOS/iPadOS planning guidance says Apple deprecated MDM-based software update workloads and removed related commands with OS 27. It directs administrators to Software Update enforcement and Software Update Settings through DDM, with enforcement based on each device’s local time zone. Policies relying on legacy MDM workloads or UTC scheduling should be reviewed.

Intune · General

In-development guidance details a Defender Safe Deployment template

Intune’s in-development guidance describes a dedicated template for Microsoft Defender for Endpoint safe deployment settings on Windows, including update channels for platform, engine, and security intelligence updates. Administrators can use the material to plan standalone Defender update rollout policies for Windows devices managed through Intune or Microsoft Defender for Endpoint security settings management.

Intune · Device configuration

Intune policy guidance lists Defender Safe Deployment and AI agent profiles

The Manage Policies page now lists Defender Safe Deployment (Preview) and Microsoft Defender AI agent runtime protection profiles. It also documents the ability to control when Windows devices receive Microsoft Defender updates, giving administrators specific profiles to review when designing Defender policy.

item.title: Intune supports 100-device eSIM activation as EPM Network settings roll out — 28 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 28 October 2026

Intune supports 100-device eSIM activation as EPM Network settings roll out

The period’s meaningful updates cover two distinct administrator concerns: Intune’s documented bulk eSIM workflow for newer corporate-owned Android devices, and Endpoint Privilege Management’s gradually available Network settings capability.

Intune · General

Bulk eSIM activation and wipe behavior documented for Android Enterprise

The updated Intune index states that administrators can activate eSIMs on up to 100 selected corporate-owned Android Enterprise devices running Android 15 or later through a carrier activation server URL. Bulk wipe preserves eSIM plans by default, while administrators can choose to remove them.

Endpoint Privilege Management · General

EPM Network settings identified as a gradual rollout

The Manage System Settings guidance now says EPM System settings (Network settings) is rolling out gradually and may not be available in some tenants. The page also adds two supporting ontology links; no administrator action is required while availability catches up.

item.title: Configuration Manager 2609 reaches all customers alongside CMG NAT and image changes — 27 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 27 October 2026

Configuration Manager 2609 reaches all customers alongside CMG NAT and image changes

Configuration Manager version 2609 became globally available on October 26, allowing all customers to install it without using the early update ring. A separate 2603 update rollup adds security and functional fixes and documents CMG migration to a supported Windows Server 2022 image, Azure Load Balancer inbound NAT rules version 2, and newer VM sizes. Advanced Analytics also expanded its schema reference with Apple accessibility and content-cache fields.

Configuration Manager · General

Version 2609 is globally available

The documentation now states that, as of October 26, 2026, Configuration Manager version 2609 is available for all customers to install without relying on the early update ring.

Configuration Manager · General

KB39169655 updates CMG migration and Azure infrastructure guidance

The version 2603 update rollup documents security and functional fixes, CMG migrations to a supported Windows Server 2022 image, Azure Load Balancer inbound NAT rules version 2, and newer VM sizes. Administrators should check Azure capacity and vCPU quotas before installation, upgrade the console afterward, and install before September 30, 2027, to avoid the inbound NAT rules version 1 retirement.

Advanced Analytics · Endpoint analytics

Advanced Analytics schema adds Apple accessibility and content-cache properties

The Ref Data Platform Schema now documents AppleAccessibility properties for supervised iOS/iPadOS 16 or later devices, plus AppleContentCache, AppleContentCacheParent, and AppleContentCachePeer properties for macOS 27 or later.

View all updates for 27 October 2026 →

item.title: Configuration Manager 2609 reaches all customers as CMG tiers adopt new VM sizes — 26 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 26 October 2026

Configuration Manager 2609 reaches all customers as CMG tiers adopt new VM sizes

Configuration Manager 2609 became globally available on October 26, 2026, while CMG guidance specifies new D2ads_v6, D4ads_v6, and D8ads_v6 sizes for the Small, Medium, and Large tiers. Intune updates add concrete guidance for AOSP referenced-app assignments and Apple device-wide VPN route enforcement.

Configuration Manager · General

Configuration Manager 2609 is globally available

The installation checklist now states that version 2609 became globally available on October 26, 2026, replacing the early-update-ring opt-in instructions. Administrators can install the update without that opt-in process.

Configuration Manager · General

CMG tiers adopt new VM sizes for 2609 and patched 2603

For Configuration Manager 2609 and Configuration Manager 2603 with KB39169655, the Small, Medium, and Large CMG tiers use D2ads_v6, D4ads_v6, and D8ads_v6 respectively. Existing deployments migrate automatically to the corresponding tiers, while earlier versions retain the previous sizes.

Intune · App management

AOSP referenced-app guidance defines assignment behavior

New Intune guidance explains how to add AOSP referenced apps without an APK or Google Play selection. Required assignments unhide apps already resident on devices, Uninstall assignments hide them, and Available assignments aren't supported. The package name is required and can't be changed after the app is created.

Intune · Apple

Apple VPN profiles gain documented Enforce Routes configuration

For device-wide VPN profiles on iOS/iPadOS and macOS, administrators configure Include all networks and Exclude local networks; Intune derives the Apple Enforce Routes value automatically. The settings don't apply to per-app VPN, and split tunneling isn't recommended with them.

View all updates for 26 October 2026 →

item.title: New Intune device page becomes default in release 2609 with updated permissions — 23 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 23 October 2026

New Intune device page becomes default in release 2609 with updated permissions

The period's main operational notice is the planned replacement of Intune's legacy device page with the new experience starting with the September (2609) release. The remaining updates document Apple VPP unlimited-license assignments and revise macOS troubleshooting guidance, including the documented check-in cadence and agent check-in procedure.

Intune · Endpoint analytics

New device page replaces the legacy default in release 2609

The Intune device page experience is scheduled to become the default starting with the September (2609) release. Device-management features remain available, but administrators need the Managed devices/Update permission and the relevant action permissions. Microsoft advises updating documentation and reviewing permissions.

Intune · General

Apple VPP apps gain documented unlimited-license assignment support

The Intune index now records that Apple Business Manager and Apple School Manager VPP apps can be assigned with unlimited licenses on iOS/iPadOS, enabling deployment across an organization without managing license quantities.

Intune · Device configuration

macOS profile troubleshooting now uses a three-stage check-in cadence

The documented macOS schedule is every 3 minutes for 15 minutes, every 15 minutes for 2 hours, and then about hourly. Administrators can use this cadence when waiting for or troubleshooting device-profile changes; no configuration change is stated.

Intune · App management

macOS agent guidance removes the Terminal restart command

The Management Agent for macOS article no longer includes the Terminal command to terminate and restart the IntuneMdmAgent process to initiate an Intune check-in. Administrators will not find that command-based method in the documented procedure.

View all updates for 23 October 2026 →

item.description:
Day in brief · 22 October 2026

PowerShell sample guidance now points to the mggraph-intune-samples repository

Intune · Device security

The Supervised page changes the reference links used in its examples guidance. The guidance on evaluating threat environment, risk appetite, and usability remains unchanged; use the updated links when validating configurations.

item.title: Intune expands Sync to iOS/iPadOS while Autopilot details MDM-provider onboarding — 21 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 21 October 2026

Intune expands Sync to iOS/iPadOS while Autopilot details MDM-provider onboarding

Intune’s comprehensive Sync device action now covers Windows and iOS/iPadOS, including configuration policies, apps, and scripts. A new Windows Autopilot article defines the limited-access request and technical onboarding path for MDM providers. Other notable updates specify CMPivot certificate-trust requirements, revise the protected-app reference list, and tie a Configuration Manager 2603 fix to update rollup KB 39169655.

Intune · General

Sync now covers iOS/iPadOS workloads

Intune’s comprehensive Sync device action now applies to Windows and iOS/iPadOS and synchronizes key workloads such as configuration policies, apps, and scripts.

Configuration Manager · General

CMPivot trust handling is version-specific

CMPivot is signed with the Microsoft Code Signing PCA 2011 certificate. Configuration Manager 2603 with the update rollup and version 2609 or later automatically add the certificate to Trusted Publishers; earlier versions require manual certificate export.

Windows Autopilot · Device enrollment

Autopilot documents an MDM-provider integration path

New guidance explains how MDM providers can request limited access to integrate their services with Windows Autopilot device association, covering prerequisites, request details, review, and technical onboarding.

Intune · App management

Protected Apps reference removes two Android and iOS entries

The reference list removes Microsoft Azure Information Protection Viewer and Microsoft Power Automate entries for Android and iOS, and updates the Fuze Mobile for Intune entry and related links.

Configuration Manager · General

Configuration Manager 2603 rollup absorbs a documented fix

The 37942646 entry now states that the update is included in Configuration Manager 2603 update rollup KB 39169655, so a separate out-of-band hotfix isn’t required after the rollup is installed.

View all updates for 21 October 2026 →

item.title: macOS lockout-timer setup and Tunnel encryption guidance lead Intune updates — 19 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 19 October 2026

macOS lockout-timer setup and Tunnel encryption guidance lead Intune updates

The period was led by two actionable Intune guidance changes: a prerequisite for managing macOS lockout timers and stronger encryption-at-rest guidance for Microsoft Tunnel container files. Other updates standardized Samsung partner-link terminology, while a Security Copilot Message Center notice was corrected and should be disregarded.

Intune · Device security

macOS setup now identifies the lockout-timer prerequisite

The setup guidance directs administrators to configure Failed Attempts Reset In Minutes in the Settings catalog before rotating the password when they need to manage the lockout timer.

Intune · Device security

Microsoft Tunnel guidance recommends encryption at rest for container files

The prerequisites page states that encryption at rest is optional but strongly recommended for files used by Microsoft Tunnel containers, with links to Linux distribution and container-platform guidance.

item.title: Windows elevation defaults remain device-scoped despite user-group assignments — 17 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 17 October 2026

Windows elevation defaults remain device-scoped despite user-group assignments

Three Endpoint Privilege Management guidance updates consistently state that Windows elevation settings policies and their default elevation responses apply at device scope, even when assigned to groups containing users. A separate Samsung Knox E-FOTA update documents a one-account-per-tenant limit and region matching requirement.

Endpoint Privilege Management · Device security

Endpoint Privilege Management defaults apply to the whole device

Windows elevation settings policy client settings remain device-scoped. The default elevation response applies to all users on the device, and assigning the policy to a user group does not make that default per-user.

Intune · Endpoint analytics

Samsung Knox E-FOTA requires one matching account and region

An Intune tenant supports only one connected Samsung Knox E-FOTA account. The account and region must match where devices are registered; otherwise, device registration can fail even when the connector reports Connected.

item.title: Windows MDM-only enrollment loses CNAME auto-discovery support January 15, 2027 — 15 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 15 October 2026

Windows MDM-only enrollment loses CNAME auto-discovery support January 15, 2027

The period’s consequential change is Intune’s planned retirement of DNS CNAME auto-discovery for Windows MDM-only enrollment on January 15, 2027. A separate partner-directory update expands setup links and adds Fleet, Iru, and Samsung Knox Manage (Compliance).

Intune · Device enrollment

CNAME auto-discovery ending for Windows MDM-only enrollment

Starting January 15, 2027, Intune will no longer support DNS CNAME auto-discovery in Windows MDM-only enrollment. Users in affected organizations will need to manually enter the Microsoft enrollment server URL; existing devices and other enrollment methods remain unaffected.

Intune · Device security

item.title: Configuration Manager 2609 sets new SQL prerequisites and retires Asset Intelligence reporting — 28 September 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 28 September 2026

Configuration Manager 2609 sets new SQL prerequisites and retires Asset Intelligence reporting

Configuration Manager 2609 is the clear story for this period. The version table records build 5.00.9152.1000 as released on 28 September 2026, with support through 28 March 2028, while the accompanying guidance establishes new SQL and ODBC gates, changes database-driver handling, removes Asset Intelligence surfaces, and narrows client support. The practical impact is concentrated in Configuration Manager infrastructure used alongside Intune.

Configuration Manager · General

ODBC Driver 18.6.2.1 and SQL Server 2017 CU2 become 2609 gates

The prerequisite-check guidance requires ODBC Driver 18.6.2.1 or later for 2609 and later, and SQL Server 2017 CU2 or later starting with 2609. Unsupported versions can block installation or upgrades, and the page identifies incompatible ODBC releases.

Configuration Manager · General

2609 installs Microsoft OLE DB Driver and drops SQL Server Native Client

Starting in 2609, Configuration Manager automatically installs the Microsoft OLE DB Driver for SQL Server and no longer requires SQL Server Native Client. Configuration Manager 2603 and earlier retain the previous Native Client behavior.

Configuration Manager · General

Asset Intelligence home-page sections and reports are removed in 2609

Catalog Synchronization and Inventoried Software Status are removed from the Asset Intelligence home page, along with Asset Intelligence reports. The earlier procedures apply only to 2603 and earlier; the updated page points administrators to the product lifecycle dashboard and Asset Intelligence client settings.

Configuration Manager · General

TRUSTWORTHY is no longer required for 2609 SQLCLR loading

For 2609 and later, TRUSTWORTHY isn't needed to load Microsoft-signed SQLCLR assemblies, including databases using SQL Server Always On availability groups. Configuration Manager 2603 and earlier still require TRUSTWORTHY to be enabled.

Configuration Manager · General

Windows Server 2012 family leaves the 2609 client-support matrix

Starting with Configuration Manager 2609, Windows Server 2012, Windows Server 2012 R2, and their Windows Storage Server editions are no longer supported as client operating systems.

item.title: Intune guidance details Graph approval coverage and RHEL 9.8 Tunnel requirements — 7 August 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 7 August 2026

Intune guidance details Graph approval coverage and RHEL 9.8 Tunnel requirements

The 7 August updates are documentation-led, but several carry operational weight. Intune’s Multi Admin Approval guidance now explicitly covers delegated actions and app-authenticated Graph calls; Tunnel prerequisites detail a manual kernel-module step for RHEL 9.8; and Collect Diagnostics publishes region-specific upload URLs. Configuration Manager also updates its SQL dependency guidance, while macOS ADE documentation flags a PSSO conflict for userless devices.

Intune · Fundamentals

Multi Admin Approval guidance covers app-authenticated Graph calls

The updated Intune guide documents MAA enforcement for delegated actions and app-authenticated Microsoft Graph API calls. Per-policy enterprise application exclusions apply only to app-auth calls, allow up to 50 applications, require second-admin approval, and are audited. Approver permissions and direct group membership are also clarified. Review service principals, scripts, third-party applications, and approver-group assignments against this documented scope.

Intune · Device security

Tunnel prerequisites call out manual ip_tables loading on RHEL 9.8

The Microsoft Tunnel prerequisites now list RHEL 9.8 with Podman 5.8.2 or later as the default and explain that the ip_tables kernel module must be loaded manually before Tunnel installation. Administrators deploying Tunnel on RHEL 9.8 should complete that step before installation.

Intune · Troubleshooting

Collect Diagnostics adds regional blob URLs and a tenant geo lookup

The Collect Diagnostics page now lists new blob storage URLs for each region and directs administrators to Tenant Status in endpoint.microsoft.com to identify their tenant’s geo and data center. Review network allowlists and firewall rules and permit the applicable URLs so diagnostics uploads succeed.

Configuration Manager · General

Configuration Manager guidance names SQL Server 2025 versions and missing MSIs

The version 2603 guidance now states that SQLSysClrTypes.msi and SharedManagementObjects.msi are no longer included in Configuration Manager media. It also documents the move from deprecated SQL Server 2014 versions to SQL Server 2025 versions, including SMO 17. Administrators relying on those files should review packaging and dependency validation.

Intune · Device enrollment

macOS ADE guidance flags PSSO conflicts on userless devices

The automated macOS enrollment guidance warns against targeting userless ADE devices with profiles that enable PSSO registration during Setup Assistant. The combination can cause unexpected enrollment behavior and loss of expected device affinity. Review profile assignments for this configuration combination.
